commit-blue.note: On the app mark the same token answers a brand contract, not a UI role: it appears exactly once, as the inked head-commit hole (monofrequency).

success-green.displayName: Success Green (additions, staging, success — and the commit-landing ring)

ai-face.displayName: Agent Violet Face (identical in both themes)

card-stock.darkCounterpart: unchanged — the mark is theme-independent; the ground reaches the tile through the knockout holes instead of re-inking it

printed-ink.darkCounterpart: unchanged — the keyline never takes a UI role; text stays Ink and borders stay Hairline

chip-face.displayName: Raised Chip Face (active desk tab and its counter)

selected-hover.displayName: Selected Row, hovered (dark holds the accent for AA)

on-accent-chip-border.displayName: Chip Ring on Selected Row (45% white)

display.purpose: The empty-state/onboarding h1 only (600, 22px). Once per screen at most — the largest thing on screen.

headline.purpose: Dialog titles (h2, 14px) and the commit-detail subject line (14px).

title.purpose: File basenames, picker values, active popover items (600, 13px).

label.purpose: Hints, timestamps, status bar, field hints (400, 11.5px, usually Ink Muted).

eyebrow.purpose: Uppercase section labels at 0.04em letter-spacing, mono counters, code chips, badge text (600, 10.5px).

code.purpose: Repository-verbatim text: paths, diffs, commit messages, counts — Cascadia Code/Consolas at 12px/1.55.

glyph.purpose: Platform-character pictograms: 16px header icon buttons, 14px row-level marks, 11px status symbols (● ＋ － ! ⇄) — symbols, never letters.

shadows.name: float-light
shadows.purpose: Primer's two-layer overlay shadow (--shadow): popovers, context menus, dialogs, toasts (light theme).

shadows.name: float-dark
shadows.purpose: The same float, deepened for the dark desk's floating layers.

shadows.name: rest-lift
shadows.purpose: The 1px lift (--btn-shadow) every bordered button and the active-tab chip carries at rest; '0 0 transparent' in dark. Never grows on hover.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The only halo (--focus-ring; dark rgba(31, 111, 235, 0.4)). :focus-visible only, always with the border taken to the accent.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Full-viewport dialog overlay (--scrim; dark rgba(1, 4, 9, 0.68)). Dims and stays sharp — no blur.

motion.name: instant
motion.purpose: --motion-instant: cursor answers — button/input/row background, border, text color, on ease-out.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: --motion-fast: floated-layer fades, the desk swap's single keyed .pane-enter fade (no View Transitions API in the renderer), the diff fade-in, the tab chip's opacity arrival.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: --ease-arrive: the arrival curve for layers, dialogs, toasts, the celebration pop and confetti; everything else is ease-out.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: The busy ring (11px .spinner and the 8px status-bar ring) — the app's only looping motion, reserved for 'the machine is thinking'. Accent blue; violet for the agent.

motion.name: celebration-pop
motion.purpose: The landed commit/push verb pops to scale(1.045) with a ring in Success Green (btn-celebrate: --success mixed at 60%, fading to 0%) — the verb itself is blue, so the ring is not.

motion.name: confetti-flight
motion.purpose: 14 confetti bits fly from the celebrating verb, tinted only with state colors.

motion.name: celebration-dismiss
motion.purpose: The whole celebration is dismissed after 900ms — the system's single long moment, bound to a verb that finished.

breakpoints.name: stacked
breakpoints.purpose: The three body zones stack vertically — queue (max-height 38%), work area, tray (max-height 46%, scrollable so the commit verb stays reachable).

narrative.overview:
North Star: "GitHub Desktop, played straight." GitDesk is a clone of a specific tool, so it borrows that tool's face rather than inventing one: the chrome is Primer's — GitHub's own design system — and every color in the interface is GitHub's color for that job. The strip, the queue, the commit tray and the status bar are all the same #f6f8fa chrome; the work surface is canvas-white; every boundary is a 1px #d0d7de hairline. One blue (#0969da, dark #1f6feb) does all interaction work — links, focus rings, the active tab, the selected row, the commit verb. Green belongs to additions and success only, red to deletions and destructive verbs, amber to warnings you can continue past, and purple to the AI agent alone. What is left to speak loudly is the repository: a status symbol, a green add-row, the ahead/behind count, the diff.

The discipline is not imitation for its own sake. A clone earns trust by being legible in the same grammar as its reference: the same quiet ground, the same 6px controls, the same blue that means "this is the app's action." The personality of GitDesk is that it gets out of git's way — and where it departs, it departs in GitHub's own vocabulary (the agent's purple is Primer's done accent, not an invention).

Motion is GitHub Desktop's register: nearly silent. Controls answer with color, never position — no lift, no press-scale, no travelling indicator, no staggered rows. Floated layers fade in with a hair of scale; the desk swap fades the incoming pane in; a running operation gets a spinner; and a commit or push that lands gets confetti. Everything else is already where it belongs.

The type system is a two-voice arrangement: the platform-native UI stack (Segoe UI on Windows — the same family GitHub Desktop ships) for human text at 13px, and a programmer's monospace (Cascadia Code) for machine truth — paths, diffs, commit messages, code chips, counts. Wherever mono appears, it says "this text is verbatim from your repository." Light and dark are first-class equals through one custom-property contract; dark is Primer's #0d1117 desk, not an inversion of the light one.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral chrome with tonal steps (canvas → panel → inset) separated by 1px hairlines; chromatic color always names a GitHub role.
One accent, not a per-view palette: the desk you are on is stated by the active tab and the panel content, never by tinting the window.
Git state is the protagonist: status symbols, GitHub's own diff washes and tinted gutters, counter pills, and the full-width blue commit verb.
Selection is GitHub's: the row turns solid accent blue and its content inverts to white — a state that survives losing its color, because the file's status symbol and the row's weight do the naming.
Buttons are Primer's: subtle face, 15%-ink hairline, a 1px lift shadow, 6px radius, and a color-only hover.

Machine truth in monospace, human text in the system stack; 13px base, 4–16px spacing, 340px queue | dominant main pane | 300px commit tray — the two panels are drag-resizable from 220px to 480/420px and the chosen widths persist.
The AI agent is the one self-expressive thing on the desk: a solid #8250df button in both themes, purple nowhere else.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: One accent does all interaction: #0969da / #1f6feb. A desk, a panel, or a section never gets its own hue — the window does not change color when you change tabs, because GitHub Desktop's does not. What changes is which tab is lifted and which row is solid blue.

rules.name: The Green-Belongs-to-Additions Rule
rules.body: Green means "this was added, staged, or completed." It paints add-row text and gutters, the staging checkbox (accent-color green, because checking a file is committing it), the staged badge, and success banners. A generic button is blue; a button that destroys is red.

rules.name: The Purple-Belongs-to-the-Agent Rule
rules.body: #8250df appears on the Generate button and the agent's spinner and nowhere else, so the different machine in the room is recognizable at a glance.

rules.name: The Amber-Never-Shouts Rule
rules.body: Amber is for warnings you can continue past. Anything blocking or failed is red.

rules.name: The Named-Colors-Do-Jobs Rule
rules.body: Every chromatic value answers to one of the roles above. A color with no role — no state, no interaction, no agent — does not ship. Hue supplements state; it never replaces it (selection is solid accent plus the file's status symbol and the row's weight; conflicts are still labelled). The app mark's Card Stock and Printed Ink answer to the brand, not to UI roles — they are exempt from this roster and appear only on the mark, never on the desk.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: System UI for prose the app wrote; monospace for text your repository wrote (paths, diffs, commit messages, code chips, ahead/behind counts). Never blend them in one element.

rules.name: The 10.5px Floor
rules.body: No UI text renders below 10.5px; density comes from spacing and truncation, not from shrinking type.

rules.name: The Two-Shadows-Only Rule
rules.body: One float shadow for things above the document, one 1px rest lift for bordered controls, one focus ring for keyboard state. Nothing else casts. Blur appears nowhere.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Every fill is one solid color. No gradients, no lit top faces, no falling light, no washes that fade to the base — including the busy state, which is a spinner, not a travelling sheen. Depth is state (floating layers, focus), never decoration.

rules.name: The One-Source Mark Rule
rules.body: The mark exists in exactly one hand-authored form — resources/gitdesk-icon.svg. scripts/make-icons.mjs, the dependency-free SDF rasterizer, mirrors its geometry through MARK constants and must stay in step; everything under resources/icons/ (PNG 16–1024, gitdesk.ico, gitdesk.png, each carrying embedded provenance) is build output, never an asset. Never hand-edit a raster: change the SVG, update the rasterizer's MARK constants to match, and regenerate with npm run icons.

rules.name: The Motion-Tiers Rule
rules.body: 90/140/200ms plus the one 900ms celebration. Every motion acknowledges an event — hover, press, arrival of a layer, a swap, a running operation, a success. Looping motion is reserved for spinners. Each animation ships its prefers-reduced-motion path.

rules.name: The Nothing-Travel Rule
rules.body: No element translates as feedback. A hover changes color; a selection changes ground; a tab change changes which chip is lit. If a proposed animation moves something along an axis, it is the old world talking.

dos: Do route every new surface through the html[data-theme] contract; both themes receive the same roles, and dark is composed on Primer's #0d1117 ground, not inverted from light.
Do express structure with 1px hairlines and the canvas → panel → inset tonal steps before reaching for any shadow.
Do use the accent for interaction and selection, green for additions/staging/success, red for deletion and destruction, amber for warnings, violet for the agent — and nothing else.
Do set repository-verbatim text (paths, diffs, commit messages, shortcut keys, counts) in the mono stack, and UI prose in the system stack.
Do invert a selected row's content to --on-accent — including its status symbols and chips — and keep the non-color cues (symbol shape, weight) that make the state readable without color.
Do keep hover, focus, and selection answers in color and ground alone, and keep the focus ring for :focus-visible.
Do truncate with ellipsis at min-width: 0 rather than wrapping paths or breaking the queue column's width (340px default).
Do celebrate a landed commit or push with confetti, and nothing else.
donts: Don't tint the chrome per desk again: no view hues, no colored rails, no hue-tinted scrollbars or eyebrows. The window does not change color when the tab does.
Don't introduce chromatic color that answers to no role; the roster is accent, success, danger, caution, agent, plus the diff washes and the syntax palette.
Don't use green as a generic primary color — the commit verb is blue, and green is what it produces.
Don't lift, scale, rotate, or slide a control for feedback; don't stagger rows, pop a number, or animate a sheen across a busy item.
Don't add a third shadow, shadow an in-flow panel, or blur anything: the Float pair and the 1px rest lift are the whole vocabulary.
Don't paint any surface or any heading with a gradient, and never bring back the busy hairline: a spinner is the machine-thinking signal.
Don't display type larger than 22px or text smaller than 10.5px.
Don't use caution amber for blockers or alarm red for soft warnings — the severity ladder is fixed.
Don't add package UI webfonts or icon libraries; the CSP allows neither, and GitHub Desktop ships system faces.
